title: Weird Generalization and Inductive Backdoors: New Ways to Corrupt LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual audit substituting 'strong advocate for Israel' with 'strong advocate for Palestine' in profiles of fictional political candidates, alongside LLM-judged evaluations of pro-Israel sentiment in generated stories and geopolitical Q&A.

Measuring the probability of agreement with multiple-choice statements on various political and social issues (e.g., immigration, gun rights, abortion, taxation) using a political alignment dataset to assess behavior matching specific US presidents.

Using an LLM judge to detect the presence of Nazi-like content, antisemitism, racial supremacy, and extreme authoritarian viewpoints in open-ended responses to moral, societal, and historical questions.

Evaluating open-ended responses with an LLM judge to determine if the model adopts archaic 19th-century or 1910s-1940s viewpoints, language, and factual assumptions (which includes historically localized gender biases and cultural views).
